sections.title: Almost-sure, probability, distribution and mean-power convergence

missing_pieces.duty: assessment_dispute: US-0: Item (6) of thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-comparison (handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex lines 215-220) claims an 'if and only if': X_n->X in probability and in L^p iff X_n in L^p for every n and (|X_n|^p) is uniformly integrable. The annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex lines 198-199) only cites thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-vitali, which already assumes X_n in L^p (parts line 231). The necessity of X_n in L^p and of uniform integrability is never argued. It is also false under the chapter's own definition (parts lines 77-78, 85-88): take X_n=X=Y with E|Y|^p=infinity; this converges in L^p and in probability, yet X_n is not in L^p and |X_n|^p is not uniformly integrable. So the named probability-to-mean comparison is not established as stated. All 70 MP/UI/WCL components and the rest of the comparison (three ranges, L^p inside L^q, a.s./probability/distribution implications, general-p Vitali, five countermodels, the 12-pair failure count, and the Durrett variants checked in the held PDF) are covered.
